source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project (IFAD-funded) - "Climate Resilient Banana Growing Technique" (ផលិតកម្មដំណាំចេកដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ), November 2018
text: The booklet closes with a blank cost-benefit worksheet template that farmers can fill in for their own plot, listing input cost categories to record: planting material (suckers/corms), fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation/water costs, labor, and transport, alongside expected revenue from bunch sales. Filling in this template with local prices is presented as a way for farmers to judge for themselves whether adopting the climate-resilient practices in this booklet (drip irrigation, bunch bagging, and the recommended fertilizer schedule) pays off on their own land, rather than relying only on the booklet's general claims about water savings and yield.
